svg.title: claudia composes — the floating object layer: every kind of object, held and let go, and Edit ▸ Image…
svg.desc: A text with a LaTeX container, a picture, a shape with words and a text box hanging at their characters; the held object's tether and chip; the held and let-go states; Edit ▸ Image… with the shared import dialog; the rule for where an object hangs; what the numbers mean and the open points.

text.font-family: Fraunces, Georgia, serif

svg.text: claudia composes — the floating object layer

For review before the wrap work. Content is invented. What you see in A is built on this branch (every kind of object drawn, at its character plus offset, let go on a click into the words); wrap is in the next mock-up.

text.font-family: Fraunces, Georgia, serif

svg.text: A · Everything that floats, hanging at its character
Flow view. Each object hangs at the character it is anchored to, moved by the offset the model keeps, and floats over the words without pushing any aside (D179).
Only the held object shows its ring and tether, so reading is quiet.

text.font-family: Fraunces, Georgia, serif

svg.text: The second quarter closed with a surplus of 4.1 percent, mostly from lower travel
costs. Two items stand out: the software licences, which are paid once a year, and
the exchange rates used for foreign invoices, which were fixed in January and
have not been looked at since.
Travel was cheaper because the autumn conference moved online. We expect the
saving to hold for one more quarter and then to disappear, since two of the three
teams plan to meet in person again in the spring.
The next step is a review of the rates before the half-year close. Tobi will collect
the invoices, and Anna will check the figures in the table against the sources.
Questions go to the finance desk.

svg.text: B · Held, and let go again
Clicking an object holds it; clicking into the words, or tabbing back into them, lets go.
The outline used to stay for good: nothing cleared the selection.

text.font-family: Fraunces, Georgia, serif

svg.text: → holds it: ring, tether and grip appear
Click or Tab into the words
→ lets go; the caret is where it was put
→ lets go; the caret comes back where it was
→ hangs it from the previous / next paragraph

text.font-family: Fraunces, Georgia, serif

svg.text: C · Edit ▸ Image…, and the one dialog
composes could not take a picture in. Now Edit ▸ Image… (Ctrl+Alt+I), as in creates
and computes. The picture hangs from the caret's character, at most 240 high
and no wider than a container.
Description (read aloud to someone who cannot see)
A tabby cat asleep on a keyboard
Decorative: only for looks, skipped by readers

text.font-family: Fraunces, Georgia, serif

svg.text: D · Where an object hangs, on the screen and in print
One rule for both, so that what is seen is what is printed, up to the small
differences between the browser's lines and the layout engine's.
left = the character's left + dx, then kept between the column's left edge and its right
edge minus the object's width. top = the character's top + dy, never above the top of the
text. Print adds what the screen does not need: the bottom margin (an object is moved up
A paragraph with nothing to measure (no words) gives its own corner. dx and dy are in the

text.font-family: Fraunces, Georgia, serif

svg.text: A LaTeX container hangs at its character. It used to be pushed against the
paragraph's right edge, whichever its anchor.
A picture, hung from the heading's last character and moved 380 across, into the
empty part of that line. No frame of its own.
A shape with words, held: the outline, the grip, the ring on the character, the
tether and the chip appear only while held.
A text box: its own box (fill, border) from its style, its words from the
paragraph style inside it. Not drawn at all before.
The anchor ring: the character the object hangs from. It follows the text through
Held, then let go: a click into the words (or Tab into them) clears the selection;
Esc lets go too, and the caret comes back where it was.
A chart: not drawn in a text yet, so it says so instead of leaving a gap (print
says the same in its notes, D907).
Edit ▸ Image… (Ctrl+Alt+I): the same entry and key as in creates and computes.
The dialog is the one of all three apps; each app only says where the picture goes

text.font-family: Fraunces, Georgia, serif

svg.text: The offset exists but nothing sets it by hand yet. Recommended: drag the
held object; the ring stays and the offset follows the pointer, snapped to
the object's own grid (D214), one step per drag. The arrow keys keep
The earlier mock put it under Insert. Edit ▸ Image… is built, because
creates and computes have it there and one entry has one key in all three
apps; Insert holds what only composes has.
creates' SlideCanvas still draws pictures, shapes and boxes itself.
Recommended: move it onto the same look (lookOf) later; not touched here.
